Cortech Barracuda Inmate Property Storage Box – 3825P / 7268P / 8568P
Cortech Barracuda Box - Inmate Property Storage Box
Stack-and-Nest Polypropylene Property Storage Box in Three Sizes for Correctional Facilities
Cortech USA 3825P, 7268P, 8568P Barracuda Box - Inmate Property Storage Box
Headings marked [H2] should be set as H2 on the page.
Cortech Barracuda Inmate Property Storage Box

gives jails and prisons a tough, lightweight box for inmate property and records. Each box is molded in one piece from high impact “no break” polypropylene, with rounded corners and edges and vertical structural columns that help it stand up to impact.

The stack-and-nest design lets you stack boxes, with or without a lid, without crushing what is inside. Turn an empty box 180 degrees and it nests inside another, which saves storage space and freight. There is a locking hasp on both sides of the box, and the matching Barracuda Box lid is sold separately.
One-piece injection-molded high impact “no break” polypropylene
Rounded corners and edges and vertical structural columns for strength and impact resistance
Stacks with or without a lid; empty boxes nest when turned 180 degrees
Locking hasp on both sides of the box
Flame retardant; passes California Technical Bulletin 133
Sold separately as the Cortech Barracuda Box Lid
Easy to clean, sanitize, and maintain
USA, made to ISO quality standards
The Barracuda Box is made for allowable in-cell storage and property rooms. With three sizes, facilities can choose the size that fits what each person is allowed to keep.
Inmate records and personal property storage

H1: your current H1 is "Cortech Barracuda Box - Inmate Property Storage Box." I changed it so it reads the same way as the Norix pages and includes the three model numbers. Is that okay?

I left out "the toughest inmate property storage box available" and "stronger, lighter and more functional than other inmate property storage boxes," since these are marketing claims that compare it with other brands.
Numbered boxes: your current page says each Barracuda Box is individually numbered. The Cortech spec sheet and web page say this only for the Master Box, so I left it out.
Dimensions: the Cortech spec sheet lists height × width × depth (for example 8.5” × 23” × 17.5”). I wrote them as width × depth × height, like the other pages. They match your current page.
Shipping weight: Cortech does not publish weights for the Barracuda Box. Your variants are set to 6, 8, and 12 lbs, which look realistic, so I left them as they are.
Product images: the page has one image (an open box). Cortech has photos of the 1.5 cu ft box, the 2.0 cu ft box, and the 3.0 cu ft box with a lid. Would you like me to add them?
9689P / 8289P: Cortech Barracuda Inmate Property Storage Box Lid
Cortech Barracuda Inmate Property Storage Box Lid – 9689P / 8289P
Cortech Lid for Barracuda Inmate Property Storage Box

Cortech USA 9689P, 8289P Cortech Barracuda Box Lid for Barracuda Inmate Property Storage Boxes
Headings marked [H2] should be set as H2 on the page.
Cortech Barracuda Inmate Property Storage Box Lid

closes off a Cortech Barracuda Box so it can be locked and stacked. The lid slides open from the short side of the box, so staff can reach more of the contents without taking the lid off, and a full perimeter stacking groove keeps stacked boxes in place.

Like the boxes, the lids are molded in one piece from high impact “no break” polypropylene. There are two sizes: a universal lid for the 1.5 and 2.0 cu ft boxes, and a lid for the 3.0 cu ft box. The box is sold separately.
One-piece injection-molded high impact “no break” polypropylene
Molded-in handles for opening and closing
Slides open on the short side of the box
Full engagement edges on three sides help prevent prying when the box is locked
Full perimeter stacking groove for stacking Barracuda Boxes
Flame retardant; passes California Technical Bulletin 133
Sold separately as the Cortech Barracuda Box
USA, made to ISO quality standards
Fits the 3825P and 7268P boxes (1.5 and 2.0 cu ft), 23½”W×17½”D×1½”H
Adding a lid lets facilities lock Barracuda Boxes and stack them neatly, whether the boxes are kept in cells or in a property room.

3825M / 7268M / 8568M: Cortech Master Box Lockable Inmate Property Storage Box
Cortech Master Box Lockable Inmate Property Storage Box – 3825M / 7268M / 8568M
Cortech Master Box - Lockable Inmate Property Storage Box
Polypropylene Property Storage Box with Built-In Combination Lock and Master Override Key
Headings marked [H2] should be set as H2 on the page.
Cortech Master Box Lockable Inmate Property Storage Box

has a built-in combination dial lock, so facilities can lock inmate property without handing out padlocks. A master override key lets staff open any box when they need to, and each Master Box is individually numbered for inmate ID and property control.

The Master Box is molded from high impact “no break” polypropylene in the same three sizes as the Cortech Barracuda Box. Rounded corners and edges and vertical structural columns help it resist impact, and boxes stack with or without a lid and nest when empty. Lids are sold separately.
Built-in tamper-resistant combination dial lock with a master override key, so no padlocks are needed
Each box is individually numbered for inmate ID and property control
Rounded corners and edges and vertical structural columns for strength and impact resistance
Stacks with or without a lid; empty boxes nest
Flame retardant; passes California Technical Bulletin 133
Sold separately as the Cortech Master Box Lid
Easy to clean, sanitize, and maintain
10-year warranty on the box; 5-year warranty on the lock
USA, made to ISO quality standards
The Master Box is made for facilities that want lockable property storage without the risks that come with padlocks.

7501 / 7502: Cortech EZ Bunk Stackable Platform Bed Sleep Surface
Cortech EZ Bunk Stackable Platform Bed Sleep Surface – 7501 / 7502
Cortech EZ Bunk Stackable Platform Bed Sleep Surface
One-Piece Molded Temporary Sleep Surface That Stacks 20 High in 7 Vertical Feet
Cortech USA 7501, 7502 EZ Bunk Stackable Platform Bed Sleep Surface
Headings marked [H2] should be set as H2 on the page.
Cortech EZ Bunk Stackable Platform Bed Sleep Surface

is a temporary bed for jails, prisons, and shelters that need extra sleeping space during overcrowding or emergencies. It is rotationally molded in one piece from high density polyethylene, with no seams or holes, and 20 bunks stack in 7 vertical feet when they are not in use.

Molded handles run along the sides and ends for carrying and stacking, and internal molded structural cones give the sleep surface strength and support. The EZ Bunk fits under most wall-mounted bunks and is designed for a 30”×75” mattress, sold separately.
One-piece rotationally molded high density polyethylene with structural and flame retardant additives
30”×75” on the primary side; the other side gives a 25”×75” secondary surface
Designed for a 30”×75” mattress, 4½” thick recommended (sold separately)
Integral full-length molded handles on the sides and ends
Tested to ISO 22196, showing a greater than 99% reduction in bacteria
Flame retardant; passes California Technical Bulletin 133 and UL 94 HB
Sound dampening, and easy to clean, sanitize, and maintain
Blue Gray (7501) or Slate Blue (7502); custom colors available on request
USA, made to ISO quality standards
The EZ Bunk is made for temporary bunking, so facilities can keep bunks stacked in storage and set them up when the population rises.

H1: I kept your current H1 and added the two model numbers.

Variant names: your variants are named "7501 - Grey" and "7502 - Blue." The Cortech spec sheet, catalog, and web page call the colors Blue Gray (7501) and Slate Blue (7502). Would you like them renamed "7501 - Blue Gray" and "7502 - Slate Blue"?

Product images: the page has two images. The first shows a dark EZ Bunk that does not match either current color, and the second shows a mattress, which is sold separately. Cortech has photos of the Blue Gray and Slate Blue EZ Bunks. Would you like me to add them?
VM1115 / VM1520 / VM1824: Cortech Ventura Acrylic Mirror
Cortech Ventura Acrylic Mirror – VM1115 / VM1520 / VM1824
One-Piece Break-Resistant Acrylic Mirror with Integral Frame and Tamper-Resistant Fasteners
Cortech USA VM Ventura Acrylic Mirror
Headings marked [H2] should be set as H2 on the page.

is a one-piece mirror made from 100% virgin acrylic, with the frame molded in. It has the look of a glass mirror without the same fragility, and it is highly resistant to breakage, which suits correctional and behavioral health facilities.

Each mirror comes with 10 tamper-resistant Torx button-head screws with center pin reject and has recessed mounting holes for secure attachment. It ships with an abrasion-resistant backing that protects the mirror surface.
100% virgin acrylic, one-piece design with integral frame
10 tamper-resistant Torx button-head screws with center pin reject, included (T25 bit)
Ships with abrasion- and scratch-resistant backing material
Clean with a microfiber cloth and non-abrasive soap and water; do not use glass cleaner
USA, made to ISO quality standards
Hold the mirror to the wall and mark the holes, drill ¼” holes 1” to 1⅛” deep for the anchors, and fit the protective O-ring between each screw and the mirror; see Cortech instructions
Do not over-tighten the screws, which can damage the acrylic
Remove the front film after the mirror is installed
The Ventura Mirror suits rooms where abuse or harsh conditions would break or damage a glass mirror.

Thickness: your current page says "236 nominal thickness" with no unit. The Cortech spec sheet and web page do not give a thickness, so I left it out.

Installation: I added the mounting and care steps from the Cortech installation instructions.

Shipping weight: all three sizes are set to 10 lbs, which looks like a placeholder. The Cortech spec sheet says "See chart" for weight but has no chart, and the Cortech web page has no weights. Would you like me to leave them as they are?
Meta title: adding "at Anchortex" would make it 70 characters, so I left it off, the same as the Norix part-number titles.
Product images: the page has one image, and Cortech has no other photos of the Ventura Mirror, so it stays at one.
